16	> before adopting anything.**

19	> Helm release Fleet has taken ownership of, deleting the path runs the
20	> equivalent of `helm uninstall`. This deleted karakeep's StatefulSets,
21	> Deployment, Service, Ingress and one PVC. Use `spec.paused: true` to stop Fleet
22	> acting, and fix forward. Only `spec.paths` removal on a bundle that never
23	> reached ownership is safe.

26	> soon as `<path>` is adopted, whether or not the child is in `spec.paths`.

# Fleet bundle — Unsloth Studio, web GUI for LLM fine-tuning (raw manifest).
# GPU-pinned to the V100 by UUID via runtimeClassName: nvidia (NOT the device
# plugin), and declared at replicas: 0 — ollama holds the same V100 with
# OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1, so scale-up is a deliberate act (see README.md).

# exist in ai (see README.md), and cert-manager + letsencrypt-dns must be live
# (Ingress hosts unsloth.ash4d.com and jupyter.ash4d.com).
defaultNamespace: ai

# Raw-manifest bundle, but Fleet still deploys it via Helm internally — so
# adopting the objects that are already on the cluster needs takeOwnership.
# Without it the first sync fails: the live objects carry no
# meta.helm.sh/release-name annotation, and Helm refuses to touch resources it
# does not believe it owns. With it, adoption is metadata-only (Helm labels on
# the top-level objects), so no pod template changes and no restarts.
# (This bundle is a fresh install with no pre-existing live objects, so
# takeOwnership is a no-op on first sync — kept for convention consistency and
# to protect a future re-adopt after a manual `kubectl apply`.)
helm:
  takeOwnership: true

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: unsloth-studio
  name: unsloth-studio
  namespace: ai
spec:
  # DECLARED AT ZERO on purpose: the GPU pin below is the same V100 that ollama
  # holds with OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1 (see 04-ollama/values.yaml), so the two
  # cannot both be resident. Scale to 1 when you want a fine-tuning session and
  # can afford to evict ollama's model (procedure in README.md).
  # Fleet will hold this at 0 — bump it here, not with `kubectl scale`, or the
  # next reconcile puts it back.
  replicas: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: unsloth-studio
  # Recreate, not RollingUpdate: the data PVC is RWO and the GPU is exclusive,
  # so old and new pods can never overlap.
  strategy:
    type: Recreate
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: unsloth-studio
    spec:
      containers:
      - env:
        # GPU pin: the Tesla V100 32GB, NOT GPU 0 (a GTX 1070, 8GB). Same UUID
        # ollama's chart pins (04-ollama/values.yaml) — that pair is the whole
        # reason this Deployment sits at replicas: 0.
        # V100 is SM 7.0: fp16 only — no bf16, no flash-attention-2. Studio
        # training runs must select fp16.
        - name: NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
          value: GPU-a69c6398-0353-3234-9f35-af0e02865f33
        - name: NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES
          value: compute,utility
        # Jupyter (and the Studio UI's auth) password. Secret is created by
        # hand, never committed — command in README.md. The image default
        # ("unsloth") must never survive: jupyter.ash4d.com is code execution
        # in a GPU pod behind this one credential.
        - name: JUPYTER_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: JUPYTER_PASSWORD
              name: unsloth-jupyter
        # Steer the HF model/tokenizer cache under the single PVC mount so a
        # pod restart never re-downloads base models. Everything that must
        # survive a restart (datasets, checkpoints, adapters, HF cache) lives
        # under /workspace/work.
        - name: HF_HOME
          value: /workspace/work/.hf-home
        # Pinned tag == the `latest` digest verified 2026-07-30
        # (sha256:f21629b9ae4e…). Upstream publishes versioned tags regularly;
        # bump deliberately, never track latest — this is a ~13 GB pull.
        image: unsloth/unsloth:2026.5.9-pt2.10.0-vllm-0.16.0-cu12.8-studio-release-v0.1.43-beta-2026-MAY-31
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        name: unsloth-studio
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8000
          name: studio
        - containerPort: 8888
          name: jupyter
        # No nvidia.com/gpu request ON PURPOSE (the 04-ollama pattern, not
        # comfyui's leftover request): requesting the device-plugin resource
        # lets the plugin inject its own NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and possibly
        # hand out GPU 0. GPU access comes from runtimeClassName: nvidia plus
        # the explicit UUID above.
        # CPU/memory bounds are for the shared 64GB/16-thread single node —
        # rationale in README.md.
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: '6'
            memory: 28Gi
          requests:
            cpu: '2'
            memory: 8Gi
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /workspace/work
          name: data
          subPath: work
      runtimeClassName: nvidia
      # The image runs as the non-root `unsloth` user; Longhorn volumes mount
      # root:root. fsGroup makes the mount group-writable for the container
      # processes regardless of the image's exact UID.
      securityContext:
        fsGroup: 1000
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: unsloth-data
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  labels:
    app: unsloth-studio
  name: unsloth-studio
  namespace: ai
spec:
  ports:
  - name: studio
    port: 8000
    targetPort: 8000
  - name: jupyter
    port: 8888
    targetPort: 8888
  selector:
    app: unsloth-studio
  # ClusterIP, not LoadBalancer: both UIs are reached over TLS through the
  # Traefik ingress below, so this does not need to burn a MetalLB IP.
  type: ClusterIP
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  annotations:
    # cert-manager issues/renews unsloth-ash4d-tls and jupyter-ash4d-tls via
    # the DNS-01 issuer.
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-dns
  labels:
    app: unsloth-studio
  name: unsloth-studio
  namespace: ai
spec:
  ingressClassName: traefik
  rules:
  - host: unsloth.ash4d.com
    http:
      paths:
      - backend:
          service:
            name: unsloth-studio
            port:
              number: 8000
        path: /
        pathType: Prefix
  # Jupyter on its own host, not a path under the Studio host — Jupyter's
  # base-URL handling under a path prefix is fragile.
  - host: jupyter.ash4d.com
    http:
      paths:
      - backend:
          service:
            name: unsloth-studio
            port:
              number: 8888
        path: /
        pathType: Prefix
  tls:
  - hosts:
    - unsloth.ash4d.com
    secretName: unsloth-ash4d-tls
  - hosts:
    - jupyter.ash4d.com
    secretName: jupyter-ash4d-tls
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: unsloth-data
  namespace: ai
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      # 100Gi: room for a couple of 13B-class fp16 base models in the HF cache
      # plus datasets and LoRA checkpoint sets. Sized against Longhorn pool
      # pressure (~412Gi of ~500Gi already allocated before this claim);
      # Longhorn supports online expansion, so grow deliberately rather than
      # over-claiming. Full-model (non-LoRA) fine-tuning checkpoints would blow
      # this budget — that workload does not belong on this pool.
      storage: 100Gi
  # Explicit — the cluster default StorageClass is local-path, so omitting
  # this is a bug (see the glm-model-pvc note in 07-comfyui/comfyui.yaml).
  storageClassName: longhorn

# 21 — Unsloth Studio

Web GUI for LLM fine-tuning (LoRA/QLoRA and full fine-tuning) on the V100,
from the official `unsloth/unsloth` image — Studio UI on 8000 at
[unsloth.ash4d.com](https://unsloth.ash4d.com), Jupyter Lab on 8888 at
[jupyter.ash4d.com](https://jupyter.ash4d.com). SSH (port 22 in the image) is
deliberately not exposed.

## Install

The Secret must exist **before** the Fleet path is enabled or the pod sticks
in `CreateContainerConfigError`:

```bash
kubectl -n ai create secret generic unsloth-jupyter \
  --from-literal=JUPYTER_PASSWORD="$(openssl rand -base64 24)"
```

Hand-test without Fleet (optional):

```bash
kubectl apply -f unsloth-studio.yaml
```

Enable via Fleet by appending this path to the live `lab-ai` GitRepo — read the
current list first and append exactly one entry (see
`14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/README.md`):

```bash
kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default get gitrepo lab-ai -o jsonpath='{.spec.paths}'
kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default patch gitrepo lab-ai --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"paths":[ <current live list...>, "21-unsloth-studio" ]}}'
```

Unlike the other `lab-ai` paths this is a **fresh install, not an adoption** —
Fleet deploys it as soon as the path lands, so the Secret and DNS
(`unsloth.ash4d.com`, `jupyter.ash4d.com` → Traefik) must already be in place.

## Image / version pinning

`unsloth/unsloth` publishes versioned tags; the pinned
`2026.5.9-pt2.10.0-vllm-0.16.0-cu12.8-studio-release-v0.1.43-beta-2026-MAY-31`
equals the `latest` digest verified 2026-07-30 (`sha256:f21629b9ae4e…`). Bump
the tag deliberately — it is a ~13 GB pull, so the first pod start on a new tag
is slow. Building a custom image (e.g. on SUSE BCI) was considered and
rejected: it would mean recreating the CUDA 12.8 / PyTorch 2.10 / Triton /
vLLM stack by hand for zero benefit.

The image is CUDA 12.8 — the host driver must satisfy CUDA 12.x compat
(`nvidia-smi` on sdf1 shows the driver's max supported CUDA version).

## GPU: replicas 0, V100 by UUID

Same pattern and same reason as ComfyUI (`07-comfyui/`): GPU access is
`runtimeClassName: nvidia` plus an explicit `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` UUID —
**not** a device-plugin `nvidia.com/gpu` request, which would let the plugin
override the pin and possibly hand out the 8 GB GTX 1070. The pinned UUID is
the Tesla V100 that Ollama holds with `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1`, so this
Deployment is **declared at `replicas: 0`**.

### Starting a fine-tuning session

1. Free the V100. Prefer the API unload over scaling ollama (Fleet will fight
   `kubectl scale` once `04-ollama` is Fleet-owned):

   ```bash
   curl http://192.168.7.153/api/generate -d '{"model":"<loaded-model>","keep_alive":0}'
   ```

   Confirm on the host that the V100 shows ~0 MiB used: `nvidia-smi`.
2. Edit `replicas: 1` in `unsloth-studio.yaml`, commit, push; Fleet's 60s poll
   picks it up. (Before Fleet owns this path, `kubectl -n ai scale deploy
   unsloth-studio --replicas=1` works too.)
3. When done, reverse: set `replicas: 0`, then load the ollama model again
   (any request to ollama reloads it).

### V100 constraints

SM 7.0 (Volta): **fp16 only — no bf16, no flash-attention-2.** Pick fp16 in
Studio's training options; bf16 runs will fail or silently fall back. 4-bit
QLoRA and fp16 LoRA both work; FP8 does not.

## Storage

One 100Gi Longhorn PVC (`unsloth-data`), single mount at `/workspace/work`
(the image's working-directory convention). `HF_HOME` is redirected to
`/workspace/work/.hf-home` so the base-model cache, datasets, and checkpoints
all live on the one PVC and survive pod restarts — the ComfyUI lesson ("both
mounts must be PVC-backed or installs die with the pod") solved with a single
mount.

100Gi fits a couple of 13B-class fp16 base models plus datasets and LoRA
checkpoints. The Longhorn pool was at ~412Gi of ~500Gi allocated before this
claim; expand online (Longhorn supports it) rather than over-claiming. Do not
run full-model checkpoint-heavy fine-tunes against this pool.

## Resources

Requests `2 CPU / 8Gi`, limits `6 CPU / 28Gi`. The node is a single 16-thread
3700X with 64 GB running everything including the k3s control plane: the low
request keeps a `replicas: 0→1` flip schedulable with ollama, milvus, emby et
al. resident; the limits cap a runaway tokenization/dataset-prep burst before
it starves the node. No GPU resource entries (see above).

## Security

Jupyter is arbitrary code execution in a GPU pod behind a single password —
the `unsloth-jupyter` Secret. Never leave the image default (`unsloth`); the
create command above generates a random one. Retrieve it with:

```bash
kubectl -n ai get secret unsloth-jupyter -o jsonpath='{.data.JUPYTER_PASSWORD}' | base64 -d
```

TLS on both hosts via cert-manager (`letsencrypt-dns` DNS-01), certs issue
even while the Deployment sits at 0 (Traefik 502s until scale-up — expected).
